topic: Brain filtering out your own nose and blinks
hook: You can see your nose right now

slides.title: It's always there
slides.body: Your nose sits in view of both eyes, every waking second.

slides.title: Your brain erases it
slides.body: Input that never changes gets filtered out, so you stop noticing it.

slides.title: Blinks vanish too
slides.body: You blink about 15 times a minute, yet never notice the darkness.
slides.image_prompt: Extreme close-up of an eyelid half closed over a bright eye, lashes catching warm light, dark background

cta: Follow for one brain fact a day
caption:
Look down a little. Your nose has been in your field of view your entire life, seen by both eyes at once. Your brain simply edits it out, because a signal that never changes isn't worth your attention.

It does the same with blinking. You blink roughly 15 to 20 times a minute, and each blink briefly cuts your vision. Your brain dims your visual processing during the blink and fills the gap, so the world never goes dark.

Follow for one fact your brain won't believe, daily. Save this and test it on a friend: did you just look at your nose?
